# Engine conformance harness specification

Status: finalized M4 specification. The harness described here is to be implemented
in M5/M6. The repository's design checker validates the plan and fixtures, not engine
execution. conformance-plan.json (not in this pack) is the traceable test catalog.

## Runner boundary and independent evidence

One versioned runner drives the same engine command/worker/adapter interfaces against
each backend. The test controller runs outside the coordinator and workers. It owns
the deterministic clock, seeded IDs, barrier schedule, independent fake-provider effect
log and temporary artifact/credential fixtures. No network model call is needed for
deterministic correctness tests. Real adapter and coding demonstrations are separate.

Each test begins with an empty isolated installation and known policy/identity fixtures,
or a named verified checkpoint produced by setup through supported commands. Injected
trusted identities are a test-host feature, never a public HUMAN field or production
endpoint. Test builds fail startup if test controls are enabled on a production listener.
All test credentials are synthetic and checked for accidental propagation to records.

The runner contract is:

| Operation | Input | Observable result |
|---|---|---|
| initialize | Case ID, seed, backend/platform/config digests, initial wall/monotonic/boot values | New installation, isolated storage/provider logs, test control channel |
| submit | Exact codec/request bytes, protected test principal context | Response or explicit transport loss; raw bytes retained with secrets removed |
| barrier | Named transaction/provider boundary, arrival count, deterministic release order | All participants parked at that boundary, or explicit watchdog failure |
| inject | Named fault point and fault type, target process/connection | Observed fault and independent confirmation of process/connection state |
| clock | Step from FAKE-CLOCK.md | Recorded clock tuple and drain observation |
| observe | Consistent committed revision/cursor and provider high-water mark | Domain projection, event chain, durable queue, ledger and provider effects |
| reopen | Same database/artifacts, new coordinator boot | Recovery state without dispatch, followed by separately requested policy evaluation |
| finish | Oracle assertions and evidence artifacts | PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED/SKIPPED report; never infer PASS from a successful process exit alone |

Observation is read-only. Expected outcomes are authored independently from the engine
reducers; snapshots generated by the system under test are not the sole oracle.
For ledger tests compare exact decimal counters and identities at every step, not just
the final balance. For external effects compare the provider's independent accepted
request log with committed dispatch responsibility. A model result saying “passed” is
not evidence. Replay uses recorded trusted time/decisions and does not call providers,
authentication, approval policies or clocks again.

A rejected user command changes no domain state or successful command event. If an
artifact/credential rejection requires an owned hold, the coordinator records a separate
authorized control transaction with its own identity and audit result. It must not
partially commit a hold inside the failed command or call that command successful.

## Backend transaction contract

SQLite and PostgreSQL run the same logical test catalog. SQLite is required for M5;
PostgreSQL remains optional/unadvertised until it passes the entire applicable suite.
SKIPPED or BLOCKED cannot satisfy that gate. Backend-specific lock errors may differ,
but public errors, committed state, reservations and responsibility must agree.

SQLite uses a single engine database on a local durable filesystem, WAL journaling,
`synchronous=FULL`, foreign-key enforcement on every connection and explicit write
transactions (`BEGIN IMMEDIATE` for admission). Read settings back; silently ignored
or weakened durability settings fail preflight. Bound busy/lock waits, then surface
retryable contention. A bounded dedicated storage executor keeps blocking database
work off the control event loop. Enable/test platform full-sync support where required
by the filesystem contract; FULL does not override a storage device that lies about
flush completion. [SQLite transaction rules](https://www.sqlite.org/lang_transaction.html)
and [durability settings](https://www.sqlite.org/pragma.html#pragma_synchronous) define
the backend mechanisms; engine invariants still require tests.

The PostgreSQL candidate uses SERIALIZABLE transactions, `fsync=on`,
`synchronous_commit=on` and `full_page_writes=on`, local durable storage and one logical
installation writer. Lock applicable ancestor/control rows in stable root-to-leaf
order (equal-depth scopes by opaque ID); unique keys protect command results, attempts,
consumer admissions and timer occurrences. Serialization/deadlock failures retry the
whole known-rolled-back transaction with fresh gates, never just its final statement.
Connection loss during commit is UNKNOWN, requiring request lookup. Queue selection
optimizations cannot bypass ancestor locks, duplicate prevention or fairness.
[PostgreSQL isolation](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/transaction-iso.html) and
[WAL configuration](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/runtime-config-wal.html) describe
these mechanisms. This is a candidate backend design, not PostgreSQL certification.

Every mutation atomically covers current workflow projection, every affected ancestor
reservation, consumed inputs, queue/timer/dispatch intent, event/outbox and command result.
No worker may observe a dispatch permit before commit. Controls such as pause, auth
epoch change and invalidation serialize against final dispatch authorization. Already
committed dispatch may still act after a later pause; it remains owned/accounted and
receives task-aware stopping. A UI must not promise that a pause undoes that permit.

## Fault boundaries and ordering

The catalog names failpoints before writes; after workflow, ancestor, queue/timer,
handoff and event/result writes but before commit; after commit before reply/outbox
delivery; before/after provider acceptance; after stop evidence; and during every
migration phase. Every applicable transaction family runs rollback/reopen checks at
each internal-write failpoint. Cases record the failpoints actually reached; failing
to reach a requested barrier is BLOCKED/FAIL, not a passed crash test.

Test both deliberate transaction exceptions and real process termination. Throwing an
exception is rollback evidence, not proof of crash recovery. Kill coordinator and worker
separately, reopen the actual database, then compare committed records and provider log.
Database-server termination and dropped connections are additional PostgreSQL cases.
Process kill is not power loss: filesystem/device fault tests require a separate VM or
storage fault harness and must be labeled accordingly. Do not run destructive power
tests against the user's working repository or real provider credentials.

For races, use independent connections and barrier-controlled simultaneous operations;
a single serialized loop is not concurrency evidence. Run both orderings of dispatch
versus pause/invalidation/policy change; reservation versus limit reduction; completion
versus artifact reclamation; duplicate consumer admission; ANY join winner selection;
owner enrollment; and timer occurrence versus cursor advancement. Preserve real-time
order when checking that outcomes admit a legal serial history. In unconstrained stress
tests any valid serial order may win; never compare arbitrary winner IDs across backends.

## Required independent oracles

| Oracle | Required assertions |
|---|---|
| Atomicity | Before commit: all state unchanged on failure. After commit: complete state/result/outbox present exactly once after reopen |
| Identity | WO/run/contract distinct; single acyclic immutable parent; operation material immutable; retries use new attempts; continuation preserves run and accounting |
| Accounting | Shared ancestors charged once per descendant attempt; dependency gates add no second charge; all cost/active/elapsed/attempt bounds and protected partition obey M3 |
| Effects | Each provider action has a prior committed dispatch; no lost-response retry creates a second unapproved effect; UNKNOWN never silently released |
| Handoff | Boundary + manifest + per-recipient delivery + input lineage atomic; receipt is not admission; exact input set admitted once; ANY cannot abandon unsettled losers |
| Human control | Both interfaces apply identical verified identity, policy, exact approval, epoch and hold checks; all resource adjustments require human authority |
| Closure | Required work/children/criteria accepted at exact revisions; all children safely closed; no unresolved exposure; canceled is not successful; terminal history stays terminal |
| Time | Equality expiry, summed active exposure, pause/downtime charging, boot fencing and bounded/coalesced occurrences match the independent clock oracle |
| Retention/restore | Live references override age; verified prefix and artifact inventory; stale backup interval held; idempotency tombstones survive archival |

Hand-calculated seed example: root cost 100, protected handoff 20, two children each
ordinary maximum 50. Racing reservations can commit only one under the root ordinary
ceiling 80. The loser records no partial child reservation or consumed attempt. Releasing
the winner before dispatch frees its 50 cost reservation but retains one consumed
attempt. A new reservation consumes another attempt. A HANDOFF reservation of 20 uses
only the protected partition and still obeys active/elapsed/attempt limits. Repeat with
dependency edges to prove they gate without adding another cost ancestor.

## Results and release gates

Each runtime report records case/version/source commit, seed, explicit ordering,
backend/version/settings, OS/architecture/filesystem, clock mode, adapter fingerprints,
failpoints reached, oracle checks and actual result. Include redacted request/response
transcripts, canonical state/event digests, effect-log digest and relevant stderr/test
exit codes as immutable evidence. Empty/missing checks cannot pass. Real and simulated
time/process/effect evidence are labeled separately. Never overwrite failed attempts
with a later successful rerun; retain both with the reason for rerunning.

M5 requires the shared deterministic and SQLite transaction/reopen tests plus an actual
approved coding workflow with real validation and interrupted recovery. M6 adds sustained
load, platform qualification, real process/storage failures, retention and restore probes.
PostgreSQL needs the same applicable evidence before advertisement. M4 completion requires
this reviewable plan and static traceability; all runtime cases remain specified-only.

## Praxis CLI first tier

The first tier of the Praxis CLI is a source-only engine profile, not wire 1.1.0. Its
workflow template, catalog, run creation and `praxis` run command cases are the WT cases
in [WORKFLOW-TEMPLATES.md](./WORKFLOW-TEMPLATES.md). The cases below cover the rest of the
first tier: the clock race and the approval window, the owner-only helper, the browser
origin and the control address, the generated host certificate and its rollover,
`praxis trust`, the catalog commands and their HTTPS client, the CLI session, the
simulated host and the `npm link` shim. The CLI session and the simulated identity
adapter are specified in [AUTHENTICATION.md](./AUTHENTICATION.md).

conformance-plan.json (not in this pack) lists these cases under `praxisCases`;
the engine spec check confirms that each names an engine test that exists.
`npm run test:engine:s6-praxis` runs every file named here and in the WT cases. The
packaged bundle's `praxis` launchers are checked by `scripts/test-engine-package-build.mjs`,
which is not an engine test and so is not listed. Second-tier cases (Tier 2 / Claim B) cover the passkey adapter, owner setup, `praxis login`, `praxis logout`, `praxis serve [--new-certificate]`, CLI session issuance, 5-minute token rotation, certificate rollover follow, fixed port 8443, and `BROWSER_ORIGIN_CHANGED`. They are verified via `npm run qualify:engine:passkeys`. First-tier cases:
